newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start with big jump, then retrace.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start with big jump, then retrace.

text.p: French shares started higher on Tuesday, supported by gains in bonds and a steady dollar, traders said. A firmer close on Wall Street also helped sentiment.
But business remained quiet as investors, particularly foreign funds, stayed on the sidelines, awaiting results of the British and French parliamentary elections.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 9.68 points or 0.38 percent at 2,559.93 at 0827 GMT, after opening up 0.82 percent.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up 1.5 at 2,556.5 from Monday's close.
Bouygues was up 2.63 percent to 546 after a positive analysts' meeting on Monday . A broker said the stock was considered cheap on a net asset value estimated at 750 francs per share.
Broker Oddo, which held its overweight recommendation, expected future earnings to be largely made up of exceptionals.

Blue chip Alcatel Alsthom gained 0.96 percent to 629, among the highest turnover stocks. Chairman Serge Tchuruk said in an interview with Le Figaro newspaper that privatisation of Thomson-CSF should not be delayed as the sell-off is vital to European defence restructuring. Alcatel is bidding against Lagardere for Thomson-CSF.
Thomson-CSF was up 0.45 percent at 177 francs.

SEB gained 2.79 percent to 1,030 after Monday's analysts meeting. The acquisition of Arno of Brazil is expected to be earnings positive by 32 million francs this year, or adding 2.2 francs per share, and by 43 million, or 2.8 francs per share, in 1998.
Oddo revised upward estimates to 38.8 francs per share in 1997 versus 36.6 previously, and to 44.6 from 41.8 for 1998.
Euro Disney was down 1.52 percent to 9.75 francs. First half losses of 210 million were in line with forecasts.
A broker said the theme park operator had been expected to post losses in the first half as it is the low season and even with gains on the operating line.
Among U.S. indicators due today are first quarter employment costs and durable goods.
The London FTSE index was at its highest level for six weeks after breaking through 4,400, just before a May 1 parliamentary election in which polls put the New Labour party as favoured to win.
